newsitem.title: UK: NatWest leads UK bank sector lower.
newsitem.headline: NatWest leads UK bank sector lower.

text.p: Shares in most UK banks stumbled on Tuesday as investors took profits after a stunning rally in the sector, dealers and analysts said.

The UK bank sector has outperformed the FTSE All-Share index by about 12.5 percent during the past six months, according to Reuters Securities 3000. The advance gained momentum just before the banks released their results.
"Banks have declared their dividends, reported results, and the market has turned a bit soggy," said one trader. "Banks have performed remarkably well and there are a lot of profits to be taken."
He said expectations that UK interest rates will head higher after the May 1 general election also encouraged profit-taking.

Shares in NatWest, still reeling from huge derivatives losses, led the decline. They shed almost 2.5 percent, or 17-1/2p, to 709, the lowest level in more than two months. NatWest shares are down about 15 percent from their February 17 peak.
"NatWest is still very much out of favour in the wake of the chaos," said one market maker.

Elsewhere, shares in Abbey National Plc fell 7p to 755-1/2p, while shares in Royal Bank of Scotland lost 9-1/2p to 548-1/2. Barclays Plc eased 6p to 1094, and Lloyds TSB Group Plc slipped 2-1/2p to 516.
Standard Chartered Plc shares bucked the trend, having underperformed the sector by about eight percent during the last six months. The shares firmed 4p to 837-1/2.
BZW analyst Hugh Pye said he viewed the recent decline in the market as a buying opportunity.
"This is just a pause in the market. Banks are still extremely cheap," he said. "We'd be using this period of price weakness to buy."
